result.output:
ATS-307 is delivered and under review.

## What was built

The repo already had a traceability **matrix** (`tests/rtm.json`, 49 rows, 1069 test references). It answers one question — "which tests belong to this requirement" — and can't answer the reverse, can't express a missing link (`TBD` is just a string), and carries no provenance. I built the traceability chain as a **DAG** on top of it, keeping the matrix in place.

**Model** (`server/traceability/`): 6 node kinds, 5 edge types, stable UIDs (`trc_1_<24 hex>` / `tre_1_<24 hex>`, same scheme family as `docs/18-UID-SPEC.md`, pure functions of kind+key), 4 provenance levels (catalog claim / source declaration / runtime record / evidence observation).

**Three decisions worth reviewing:**
- **No reverse edges.** Storing `evidence→testcase` would create `evidence→testcase→run→evidence` cycles, making the "cycles are checkable" acceptance point meaningless. The backward walk is a reverse traversal of the forward DAG.
- **Shared-node binding lives on the edge.** Design anchor `B04` is shared across requirements, so walking back through it reached FR-008 from FR-007's evidence. This was a real bug my probe caught mid-implementation; the requirement binding now sits on the `covers` edge.
- **`no-script` ≠ `no-declaration`.** ST probes don't carry case IDs, so they connect only via the catalogue's `evidence` field — a weaker link than a declaration. Collapsing them would report real implementations as absent.

## Verification

UT 33 + IT 9, full regression **1865 pass / 0 fail**, negative control confirming the checks actually go red on 4 kinds of corruption. On the real tree: orphan edges 0, cycles 0, absent nodes 0, dangling test ids 0, dangling anchors 0.

**One finding surfaced, not hidden:** 88 cases the catalogue declares `PASS` have no script declaring those IDs — the implementations use a different ID scheme (`ATS-202-UT-001` vs `UT-DSC-001`). Unifying those is separate work; the graph reports the drift rather than papering over it.

## Not done

No UI (ATS-310), no incremental/impact API (ATS-309), and the runtime-run join was only exercised via the transcript path. ST itself remains unexecuted — its gaps show as `no-run`, which is gap visibility, not a PASS.

## Delivery

Branch `agent/m3/seikoist-183` at `11fe4b7`, merged into `dev` as `155a46e` (conflicts in the binary `docs/WBS.xlsx` and the generated manifest resolved by taking `dev` and re-running the updater — both ATS-307 and ATS-403 rows verified intact). WBS row 47: 待审核 / completion1 / remaining 0. Comment posted, assigned to Opus, status `in_review`.

ATS-213 is complete and delivered.

## What was delivered

**Scope:** ATS-402 already delivered credential *storage* (secret → OS credential store, index holds only a reference, no plaintext fallback). The gap was that the UI could show "N references" but **not whether any of them still works** — and the index and the credential store drift apart. So ATS-213 delivers the **availability status surface** plus a real leak fix.

**Credential status** — a closed three-value set, exactly one per reference: `configured` / `not-configured` / `unavailable`. The status is **measured against the OS credential store, not inferred from the index** — verified by deleting the entry from the real Windows Credential Manager while the platform index kept the reference (status correctly read `not-configured`, index still referenced it). "Not configured" and "unavailable" are kept separate (re-enter the secret vs. fix the environment), and retrieval failure reports a closed reason-code vocabulary rather than degrading silently.

**A real leak found and fixed:** V8's `JSON.parse` error message carries a fragment of the raw input, and `POST /api/security/credentials` puts the secret in that body. Measured: the secret's first 10 characters reached the HTTP response body. Now reported as `INVALID_REQUEST_BODY`.

The wakeup was one-shot (`mode: once`, `fire_count: 1`) and already disabled — no recurring work to disable. The branch is clean, and `dev` has the merge.

## ATS-111 delivered

**Four states, distinguishable** — a single model (`apps/studio/lib/workbench-state.mjs`) defines empty / error / cancelled / loading as a *closed set* with a total mapping. Each carries its own label, detail, "what to do next", ARIA role and politeness — four different words, never colour alone. Cancellation is real: `cancellableApi` (AbortController) in `lib/api.ts` lets Esc abort an in-flight load, and the panel then says 「已取消」, not 「加载失败」. An unrecognised outcome is reported as a *failure*, never as "nothing to show".

**Core flow keyboard-completable** — Esc cancels, Enter submits, Ctrl+Enter runs, Ctrl+P focuses search. Skip link first, visible focus ring (the base stylesheet had `outline:none` with no replacement in three places), focus order calibrated to the *measured* DOM order. The add-project dialog is now a real form, so Enter uses the browser's native submit.

**Evidence** (`docs/evidence/ATS-111/`): 36 UT · 1685-item regression, 0 failures · **36/36 ST** in real Chromium · 10/10 mutations caught · static export build · 32 WBS updaters coexist · ATS-301 gate green. The four states are produced one at a time by really doing them — an actually-empty project, an injected 500, a hanging request, a reader really pressing Esc — and the core flow runs keys-only.

**One real bug found by the ST probe:** the abort handle was in React state, so `setCatalogueAbort(()=>controller.abort())` made React *call* it — every catalogue request aborted the instant it started and the panel stuck on "loading", so three of the four states could never render. Moved to a ref. Exactly the "model right, UI wrong" case only a browser finds.

**Committed and merged back to `dev`** (`cb742ca`), `WBS.xlsx` resolved by taking dev's version then re-running the updater, checksums regenerated after the merge, and everything re-verified on dev's own tree. Issue is `in_review`, assigned to Opus.

Two things I did not do, both stated in the comment: **no screen-reader was run** (the assertions are about ARIA semantics, not NVDA/JAWS behaviour), and the **portable UI** (`fallback.html`) was left alone since the scope was the Next workbench.

All gates green on the delivered `dev`. ATS-403 round 2 is delivered.

## What I did

**Resolved the inherited merge conflict first.** The unmerged state was a broken merge (MERGE_HEAD missing), so git could never complete a 3-way merge — only 9 hand-checked-out paths had landed. Provenance showed ours ≡ merge base and theirs ≡ `dev@05b5400` byte-for-byte, so the whole set went to `dev`'s side. But that only recovered 9 paths: **98 files that existed only on `dev` had been silently dropped.** I found them by diffing three trees (pre-merge branch / `dev` / mine), confirmed none were authored by this branch, and restored them. A second alignment pass fixed stale files the merge had kept from the old base (`server/env/profiles.mjs` was missing ATS-213's credential-reference feature, failing 9 ATS-214 tests).

**Implemented all 8 required fixes.** Egress payload now binds to the consent (the provider receives `verdict.inputs`, never the caller's content); `/api/ai/complete` rejects ad-hoc provider lists; provider configs are fully validated before persisting and request headers became an allowlist; provider-echoed secrets are redacted; `executeSteps` was fixed and wired up; the remaining deadline is divided across providers; the status table is corrected and now published by the code (`/api/ai/contract` `statusByCode`); the false "contract convergence (ATS-401)" claim is deleted. The three vacuous tests were rewritten as real ones.

**Turned every counterexample into a regression case** — `tools/ats403-probes/probe-ai-round2.mjs`, 23 checks + 4 negative controls. Opus's own `r1.mjs`/`r1-api.mjs` now report `not-reproduced` for P1–P7 and S1–S4.

**Two evidence-integrity bugs fixed** (both would have made my own evidence report false green): `capture-evidence.sh` ran commands inside a pipeline subshell, so `rc=$?` never reached the caller — the ATS-101 port audit was exiting 1 while the script printed "RESULT: OK". And `docs/16-BASELINE-ADR.md` §3.1 omitted a file the ATS-214 batch added. Both defects exist on clean `dev`; I fixed them because they would have masked ATS-403's own results.

## Verified vs not

Verified: UT 75/75, IT 20/20, boundary probe 37, round-2 probe 23, full suite **1846 tests / 0 failures** on the merged `dev`, checksums 1029 entries / 0 mismatches, WBS row `待审核`/1/0. Merged to `dev` as `89cbe8f`.

Not verified, stated as such in the comment: real model + real key end-to-end (never executed — no real credentials); ST-032 capture (still PENDING, no real endpoint); egress-to-destination binding (out of ATS-403 scope, flagged for a follow-up); ATS-401 contract-layer wiring (not implemented); runtime isolation; macOS/Linux credential store.

One nuance worth flagging: Opus's `r1-api.mjs` S4b now *throws* on this tree — its `/api/ai/complete` call is correctly refused with 400, so no `egress.granted` record exists and its `.at(-1)` hits `undefined`. That's the probe's own precondition no longer holding, not a product defect; the same assertion passes in `IT-AIE-020` and probe `S4b` with correct preconditions. I documented it rather than papering over it.

Issue is `in_review`, assigned to Opus.

## What the failure actually was

The delegated task `01a1bf23` was **not** a development task — it was a dependency-gate check for SEIKOIST-208 (ATS-413), triggered when ATS-402 reached terminal state. It died in `environment_prepare_failed` from host resource exhaustion (`Out of memory, malloc failed` + pack read failure), produced nothing (`delivered_comment_ids: []`), and **ATS-413 still can't start** — it waits for ATS-410, which is still `backlog`. Re-dispatching the work would have failed again for the same reason, so I re-armed the consumed wakeup rule instead (its condition was still true, so the platform would never re-fire it on its own). The re-arm already fired: a new run `01a1c168` is queued on M2.

## The merge was a bad merge-base, not a real conflict

The platform merged the user's local edits using `96d6356` as merge-base when the true merge-base is `be6b478`. That made dev's ATS-103/215/403/603/606 deliveries look like "ours deleted them" — **~95 files** were missing from the merge result. All four conflicted paths had `ours` byte-identical to the true merge-base, so taking dev's side lost nothing.

Critically, the user's local copy was an **older snapshot**, not newer intent: `probe-maestro-compat.mjs` was byte-identical to the pre-fix commit `0cbb90d`, missing dev's guard that treats "Maestro produced no output" as *inventory not verified* rather than *command exists*; the ATS-606 evidence logs predated that fix; the FR-035 line was byte-identical to dev's. 1. **Pagefile is pinned to 8 GB on C:** — `InitialSize = MaximumSize = 8192 MB`. Needs admin rights; it's the root cause of the resource-exhaustion failures.

result.output:
ATS-103 round-4 rework is complete and submitted for review.

## What the round-3 review asked for, and what I did

**D1 — the cross-origin run's exit code no longer equalled the conclusion.**
The base-resolution assertion now checks *the host the product's own resolution rule implies for the page's origin*: relative base (→ the page's own origin) when the page sits on the default port, absolute base otherwise. That keeps the same-origin run an **executable discriminator** (B and B2 still turn it red) while making the cross-origin run a **correctness check** (the absolute base is the only workable target there, so correct ⇒ green).

- Cross-origin `05b`: `RESULT: OK -- 8/8 checks passed.`, `PROBE_EXIT=0` (was 7/8, exit 1)
- Same-origin `05`: still 8/8, exit 0
- `docs/22` §1/§2.1/§2.2/§3.3.1 rewritten — "跨源 7/8" is gone

**D2 — the mutation A′ log was polluted by a busy port, and the number the doc cited didn't exist in the committed log.**
Root cause, measured (not assumed): on Windows, `TerminateProcess` (`child.kill()`) leaves the listening socket as a **zombie** — `LISTENING` with owning PID 0, blocking `bind()` for a moment. This is *not* TIME_WAIT: a server socket in TIME_WAIT still binds fine, so port availability must be decided by a real `bind()`, not by reading the socket table. Plus: the probe killed only the Bridge (its Playwright/Chromium descendants survived), and no step waited for the port.

Fix: new `tools/ats103-probes/lib/port-free.mjs` (wait for bindable / kill the whole tree / wait for release), wired into both probes and every mutation segment. The reproducing sequence went from **34 × `already in use`** (18 of 25 checks failing on the port) to **0**; A′ is now `RESULT: FAILED -- 24/25 checks passed.` with the file-tree assertion (`found: api/session`) the only red one, and `docs/22` line 60 reads verbatim from the committed log.

**One thing I corrected rather than accepted:** the reviewer's guess that descendants inherited the listening socket does not hold — they survive but don't hold it (the port frees in 15–49 ms after the Bridge dies). The doc says so explicitly so the next fixer doesn't chase the wrong cause.

## Verification

`npm test` 1646 / 0 fail (parallel and serial) · build gate 8/8 · port audit OK · ADR citations OK · checksums OK (913 entries) · four clone verifications (branch + merged `dev`, genuine CRLF and LF checkouts) all 8 steps green. `docs/22`'s output blocks match the committed logs line-for-line.

I also fixed a defect in the evidence script itself: the "LF clone" was actually still CRLF, because `git clone -c core.autocrlf=false` configures the clone *process*, not the new clone. Now written into the clone's own config (CR byte count: 118 vs 0).

**Merged to `dev` at `98f568e`** with `--no-ff`; branch and dev are the same commit, tree clean, **zero product-code changes**. WBS row: 待审核 / 1 / 0. Issue set to `in_review`, assigned to Sonnet.

Two caveats I logged rather than papered over: the zombie-socket root cause and the non-Windows branch of `port-free.mjs` were only exercised on Windows 11.

## 改了什么

**J1 —— 越界判定改为按解析后的真实路径做**（`server/evidence/manifest.mjs`）

原判定是词法的：`lnk/state.json` 字面上在 run 目录里，但 `lnk` 是指向数据目录的 junction，解析后它就是数据目录的 `state.json`。现在每条目解析真实路径再判定，越界的被拒绝并记入 `rejected[]`，校验与清理都不跟随。两个边界按复核要求处理：文件已不存在时按**最深的存在祖先**解析（仍是「缺失」而非「越界」）；锚点是「按 run id 得到的 run 目录」本身，不是它 realpath 之后的结果。`results/` 是目录链接时只摘链接，不删链接所指的树。

**M1 —— 清理记录只增不减**：新记录与旧记录合并，删除的事实一旦记录就不被撤回。

## 结论

Opus 的第 1 轮 REJECT（探针 `0/8 OK`）列了 7 项必改项，已逐条处理。**复核探针在合并后的 dev 树上 `RESULT: 8/8 OK`**。

**核心的三处改动：**

1. **未出结论的运行不再污染判定指标** — `cancelled`/`error`/`interrupted`/未知状态的用例现在在所有指标更新**之前**就 `continue`，不进任何判定桶、attempt 桶、重试计数和跨运行视图，单列为 `inconclusive`。这修掉了「取消的运行里失败过的用例，把一个通过的用例判成不稳定」这个根因。

2. **跨运行身份不再合并不同的用例** — 适配器把模型算出的身份（describe 路径 + 行号 + case key）存进摘要，模块据此区分同名的两个用例；摘要不带身份时退回「文件+标题」，此时撞键的条目标记 `ambiguous`、不贡献判定，不静默合并。

## Dependency check → promotion

`tools/wbs_ready.py --list` confirmed ATS-209's only prerequisite is ATS-208 (`done`), so the task was promoted `backlog → todo` and worked. Not merely the trigger's partial signal — the full prerequisite set was re-verified.

## What was delivered

An Evidence Manifest + SHA-256 + dedup/retention subsystem (`server/evidence/`, 4 modules, ~96–99% line coverage), wired into the bridge, plus a design doc, 39 UT + 10 IT, a probe, and 8 evidence logs.

Both acceptance criteria have real implementations and measurements:
- **Tampering detectable** — `verifyEvidence()` recomputes each digest and reports `missing` / `changed` / `extra` separately, naming the file and both digests.
- **Retention expiry cleans without deleting Run metadata** — the cleaner removes only evidence files from run folders; `events.jsonl`, `stdout.log` and `manifest.json` stay, and the run record (status/summary/attempts/events) lives in `state.json` and is untouched — proven by a field-by-field comparison.

Three design decisions worth flagging: the manifest is a *function* of the run and its folder (so it can be rebuilt and compared) and now carries `projectUid`/`sourceCommit` — v1 recorded digests without saying which run they belonged to; digests are over raw bytes with **no** line-ending normalization (normalizing would hide exactly the kind of rewrite evidence must detect); and deduplication uses **hard links**, so bytes are stored once and the copies cannot diverge — which is what tamper detection relies on.

Opus's rejection was correct, and the root cause was one design error with four visible faces: **the anchor was treated as a stronger signal than it is.** The anchor says "which render number" — a fact about a *position*, not about a *case*. |---|---|

| 2 | Took option (A): the ordinal counts the **CLI's report order**, not the title-sorted rank (a re-worded title changes its rank). `parseListReport` now records `reportOrder`. |
| 3 | Matrix `caseKey` carries the describe path, matching `parseListReport` exactly. |
| 4 | `parseReport` carries the describe path into `attemptsForRun`'s `scope`; signal 2 is live, step 2 does the body check, and the dead `!positionMismatch` test is gone. |

Wakeup 01a1af56-9593-7aef-9950-a861fd195583 triggered. Instruction:
ATS-601（移动端执行目标抽象与设备/模拟器会话模型）开工。

## 为什么现在做这一项

用户提出 Maestro Studio 的管理模式值得借鉴——平台也要能测 App。移动端执行面已作为 **S6 / v0.5.0** 新阶段纳入 WBS（ATS-601~606），设计书见 `docs/25-MOBILE-APP-TESTING.md`（已在 `dev` 上，合并提交 `72a77da`）。

**你是这一阶段的第一项**：先冻结目标抽象与用例模型契约，后面 Android Runner（ATS-603）才不会变成第二个 Playwright 专用实现。

本任务**没有前置依赖**，可直接开工。

## 本轮要做的

1. **目标与会话模型**（设计书 §3）：
   - `Target { targetId, kind, platform, osVersion, capabilities[], declaredBy }` —— 「在哪里执行」的静态描述；
   - `Session { sessionId, targetId, state, capabilities[], lastSeenAt, error? }` —— 「当前连着的那台设备」。
   - `kind` 三取值：`local-emulator`（本平台创建与销毁）、`local-device`（已连接真机，平台只借用，**不接管安装与配对**）、`remote-farm`（远端设备农场，租约式；租约过期必须回收，复用 ATS-502 的租约语义）。
2. **状态机**：`idle → created → running → idle`，异常路径进 `failed`。硬规则：目标不存在 / 设备未连接 / 能力不满足 ⇒ **明确拒绝**（`REMOTE_TARGET_UNAVAILABLE` / `REMOTE_CAPABILITY_MISSING`），**不得静默降级**成别的执行方式。
3. **能力协商**：步骤类型与目标能力的匹配在**执行前**完成，产出「本次执行的能力缺口清单」。至少覆盖：`launchApp`→`app.install`/`app.launch`、`tapOn`→`ui.tap`+`ui.hierarchy`、`assertVisible`→`ui.hierarchy`、`takeScreenshot`→`screen.capture`、`recordScreen`→`screen.record`、`readLogs`→`log.read`。缺 `ui.hierarchy` 时 `tapOn` **不可用**——不能用坐标盲点。
4. **必须是既有契约的扩展**：ATS-301 的 RunnerAdapter/ReporterAdapter 契约是自然扩展点，**不要另起一套**。设计书 §1.3 给出了这一阶段的依赖图。
5. **安全边界**（设计书 §9）：App 包名只允许项目登记过的；Flow 文件与其它脚本同一套可信仓库判定（ATS-113），未可信项目不得执行；设备只允许用户显式登记的会话；证据落盘与其它证据同一套路径校验与 SHA-256。
6. **交付形态**：本项是**契约层**——设计 + 契约测试，**不需要真实设备**。用假会话/假目标做能力协商与拒绝规则的 UT。真实设备相关留给 ATS-603。
7. 补 UT（能力匹配、拒绝规则、状态机迁移），新建 `tools/update_wbs_ats601.py`（按 `tools/update_wbs_ats401.py` 的模式，并同步 `tools/wbs_common.py` 的 `MARKERS`）同步 WBS 行。
8. 同步 `docs/25-MOBILE-APP-TESTING.md` §3 与实现一致（设计可超前于代码，但不得把设计中的能力称为已实现）。

## 约束

- **磁盘**：C 盘刚回收 9.7 GB（现约 18.9 GB 可用）。`TEMP`/`TMP` 指到 `D:`。
- 提交顺序：先提交内容 → `python tools/update_checksums.py` → 再提交清单。
- `docs/WBS.xlsx` 是二进制共享文件，用 `tools/update_wbs_ats601.py` 改，不要用 openpyxl 另存。
- 合并回 `dev` 用 `--no-ff`，证据必须在**合并后的树**上采集。
- 本任务分支 `agent/m3/seikoist-235`（issue SEIKOIST-493 的编号）；若该分支已存在，先把最新 `dev` 合进来。

## 交付

按本 issue 描述的「完成证据」4 步：改动落在本任务分支并合回 `dev`；按「审查,UT」给出实际执行输出；同步 WBS 行的状态/完成率/剩余人日；把本 issue 置 `in_review` 并留言（结论摘要、关键证据、已验证/未验证项，末行 `Original executor: M3`），交 Opus 复核。**不得自行置 done。**

result.output:
Everything is verified and delivered. Summary of this run:

## What I found

The issue was already `in_review` from a prior round-3 delivery, but Opus posted a **round-3 REJECT** (`01a1b102`) while my run was starting, with one narrow item (R1). I independently re-verified the whole prior delivery first (all 7 reviewer probes, full suite, gates, checksums, and the "defect cases are red on the old baseline" claim Opus had flagged as N4) before touching anything — the N4 fix was genuinely in place.

## The R1 defect

WDIO same-titled entries `[skipped, failed]` / `[failed, skipped]` merged into **1 `passed` case** with `failed=0`, while the engine exited nonzero. Two independent leaks, so both needed closing (Opus: "只改分组不够"):

1. **`aggregateOutcomes` dropped `unknown`** — `expected` is a claim about *every* outcome, so a list holding an `unknown` cannot make that claim. WDIO declares no expectation, so `skipped + unknown` was read as `expected`, and the status aggregation rewrote `failed` → `passed`.
2. **WDIO grouping ended only at a *passed* entry** — a skipped test isn't retried either, so an entry after a skipped one is a different test.

## Verification

- R1 probe: `RESULT: 0 failed` on the delivered tree, `4 failed` on the pre-fix tree.
- All 8 reviewer probes pass; new `UT-EXE-032` is red on `08713a1`, green after.
- Full suite **872/872** on the merged tree; coverage all >90%; python gates 42/42; ATS-301 + `verify_checksums` → OK.
- One full-suite failure set in the shared `D:/ICHOR` checkout was **port contention with a concurrent agent** — the same file passes 14/14 in isolation and 872/872 on an isolated export. I said so explicitly in the comment rather than reporting it as a product defect.

## Delivered

Branch `agent/m3/seikoist-169-3111785a4ef3` (R1 fix `82340dc` → evidence → WBS → checksums → dev-tree gates), merged `--no-ff` into `dev` (`889a427`, checksums regenerated `89de90a`). Docs `24`/`06` and the WBS row updated for the changed rules. Comment posted with evidence, assigned to Opus, status `in_review`.

One note: `UT-EXE-030` had an assertion encoding the *old* rule (`aggregateOutcomes([unknown, expected]) === expected`), which R1 explicitly reverses — I changed it and documented why in the commit and the review comment rather than leaving the two rules in contradiction.

This run continued **SEIKOIST-169 / ATS-208** after a **review REJECTION**. The reviewer (Opus) had found 8 mandatory defects; all are now fixed, verified, merged to `dev`, and re-submitted for review.

**What was wrong and what changed**

- **B1 — verdict semantics were inverted.** The model judged cases by raw attempt status, so a `test.fail()` case counted as `failed` while Playwright exited 0. Added a second vocabulary (`outcome`: expected/unexpected/flaky/skipped/unknown) driven by the engine's `expectedStatus` and per-project verdicts. The reviewer's own probe went from **4/10 mismatches → 0/10**, and the summary now matches Playwright's `stats` exactly.
- **B2/B3/B4/B5 — recovery was fragile.** A missing run folder crashed the Bridge on every start; a torn log tail made `/events` and `/replay` return 500 forever; a terminal event was still followed by `run.interrupted`; a run stuck in `cancelling` never released its project lock. Recovery is now driven by the durable log, degrades instead of crashing, validates the state machine (`valid`/`violations`), and covers `cancelling`.
- **B6 — coverage.** Each defect is now a UT/IT, plus 5 negative cases for `verifyMirror`'s event comparison. Every server file this task touched is **>90% line coverage** (model 99.31, playwright 99.47, wdio 97.50, import 95.92, core 94.12, index 93.51).
- **B7 — docs claimed things that weren't true.** The `docs/04` §3 state diagram disagreed with `RUN_TRANSITIONS`; it's now aligned and guarded by `UT-EXE-028`, which fails if the diagram drifts again.
- **W1 (non-blocking)** — WDIO's retry merge never worked; it now does, based on a measurement of the real `@wdio/reporter` 10.1.0.

Done. ATS-102's 3rd rejection is addressed and resubmitted for review.

## What the rejection was

One required fix: the installed-tree digest hashed **raw bytes**, so it depended on the checkout's line-ending style. npm writes the hidden lockfile `node_modules/.package-lock.json` in the line-ending style of the `package-lock.json` it read — 752 CR under a CRLF checkout, 0 under LF. The recorded value therefore only held for the checkout it was measured in, and the mismatch message pointed at "lockfile is wrong" when it wasn't.

I reproduced this independently before fixing it: clone A's raw sha256 `fa2fd4ea…`, LF-normalized `6df2c174…` — matching the reviewer's figure exactly.

## The fix

`tools/tree_digest.mjs` now hashes text files (no NUL in first 8000 bytes — git's own rule) with CRLF normalized to LF, and binary files byte-for-byte. Three details that matter: binary detection runs *before* any hashing (otherwise the result depends on read order), CRLF pairs split across the 64 KiB read boundary are stitched with `pendingCr`, and a lone CR is preserved — it isn't a line ending.

## Verification| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| CRLF vs LF clone, `all-files` digest | **identical** — `0915e9b2…`, both `--check` exit 0 |
| Hidden lockfile raw sha | `fa2fd4ea…` vs `6df2c174…` — differs, as it must |
| Unit test (new, 10 assertions) | 10/10 — incl. corruption still detected |
| 8-step gate on final tip | exit 0, 165 tests / 158 pass / 0 fail / 7 skip |
| 8-step gate on merged `dev` (fresh clone) | exit 0, clean tree |

The previous run had already written and merged the code but **died before posting its conclusion** (two `HTTP 429 Token Plan 用量上限` system comments on the issue). So this turn was independent re-verification plus the missing conclusion — not a redo.

The inherited docs cited **two digests a third party could not recompute**:

- `2ece6ea6…` (install-tree aggregate) — its recipe was never recorded. I tried ~2000 combinations (path prefixes, separators, sort orders, line endings, case, raw-vs-hash) and none reproduced it.
- `3314e0e7…` (`tsconfig.json`) — that value **does not exist in any historical version** of that file in the repo.

I withdrew both explicitly (with the reason recorded) and replaced them with `tools/tree_digest.mjs`, which states the recipe in its file header, plus `tools/installed-tree-digests.txt`. The check is now wired into the CI workflow and the local gate.

Two things I got wrong in my own first implementation and fixed: the tool buffered whole trees and crashed with `RangeError` under memory pressure (now streams per file), and I initially treated the digest as platform-independent — it isn't, since the lockfile declares 34 platform-specific optional packages and npm installs only the host's. Expected values are now per platform, and a platform with no baseline skips rather than fails.

6-step gate green on a fresh clone (exit 0), 59/59 tests, working tree clean, lockfiles unmutated. The new gate also caught a real install corruption that `npm ci` did **not** — a truncated, zero-padded `image-optimizer.js.map` while npm exited 0 and the tarball integrity check passed.

GitHub Actions never ran on a real runner (remote `main` has only a LICENSE; branch unpushed) — workflow correctness rests on local reproduction. Rust/Tauri build, the NFR-012 distribution audit, full SPDX SBOM, macOS/Linux, and build-step crash rate all remain unverified.

Everything is in place. The assignee is now Opus (a different agent ID), status is `in_review`, and the result comment is posted.

**SEIKOIST-217 delivered — ATS-501 远程 Runner 边界、威胁模型与协议冻结**

**What was delivered** — `docs/18-REMOTE-RUNNER-PROTOCOL.md` (454 lines) freezing the remote execution plane's five acceptance elements: a four-plane trust model with 8 hard-boundary rules, one-time enrollment token + Ed25519 request-signature authentication, major-strict/minor-floor/capability-by-name version negotiation, server-derived tenant context with cross-tenant 404 masking, 24 `REMOTE_` rejection codes under a deny-by-default policy, 13 STRIDE threats, and ADR-015~020. Plus a machine-readable constraint block and a 64-assertion audit probe that checks the prose and the block agree in both directions.

**Verified** (real output in `docs/evidence/ATS-501/`): contract audit 64/64, `npm test` 20/20, `node --check`, port audit OK, WBS coexistence 5/5, CHECKSUMS 86 entries with 0 mismatches.

**Not verified** — stated plainly in the issue comment: the remote plane has no implementation in the repo, so no runtime behavior was verified. The only executable evidence is the document's own consistency check. FR-028/FR-030 stay `DESIGNED`.

**Two pre-existing defects fixed along the way**: the two WBS updaters each hardcoded the overview's cached totals, so the later one reverted the earlier one's result — now derived from the sheet with per-task marker blocks. And the updaters unconditionally rewrote their row to 待审核, which would have undone an already-accepted review on re-run — now they only write it when the row isn't already terminal.

**Two deviations flagged for Opus**: the document is numbered 18 because `dev` already gave17 to ATS-401's agent contract; and this branch sits on `fa881fe` rather than `dev`, because rebasing onto `dev` dropped the required starting commit. The marker-block mechanism is implemented and tested for three-way coexistence, so the merge with `dev` is left to integration.

Branch `agent/m3/seikoist-217`, 4 commits on top of `fa881fe`; ATS-501's WBS row is set to 待审核 (not 已完成) pending review.

ATS-401 is delivered and submitted for Opus review.

## What was built

**Agent 契约 v1** (`agent-contract/v1`) in `server/agent.mjs` — the deliverable the WBS calls for. The two acceptance criteria are enforced as *mechanisms*, not conventions:

- **Requests carry scope, budget, provenance** — `scope` (absolute root, no path escapes, `outputs` restricted to test scripts), `budget` (4 required fields, platform-capped), `inputs` (kind/ref/sha256-digest/content, digest recomputed before the provider is called).
- **Cannot save or commit test scripts** — guaranteed by four independent mechanisms: the contract layer imports only `node:crypto` and `node:path` (physically unable to write files, spawn processes, or reach the network); 11 write/commit capabilities are rejected at the request layer; proposals are always `approval: pending` and the producer cannot review its own work; diff targets must be in `scope.outputs` *and* be test scripts.

Also: `GET /api/agent/contract`, `POST /api/agent/validate` (validate-only — never calls a model, never writes the project), 25 stable error codes mapped to HTTP 400.

## Evidence

- `npm test` → **59/59 pass** (20 pre-existing, no regressions; +28 `UT-AGT-*`, +11 `IT-AGT-*`)
- `tools/ats401-probes/probe-agent-boundary.mjs` → exit 0. Uses three independent signals, including a **negative control** that proves the static-import detector actually fires on deliberately broken source copies rather than passing vacuously.
- The ATS-101 port-audit gate caught my line-number shift in `server/index.mjs` and correctly reported `RESULT: MISMATCH`; I updated the 2 port entries and all 8 `file:line` references in the docs, each verified to point at the same construct.

## Boundary I did not cross

FR-024/FR-025 remain `DESIGNED`. No model provider is connected, and there is **no** code path anywhere that writes model output to a repo, updates expected results, or creates a Git commit. I verified this by grep and stated it explicitly in every document I touched, so the contract layer can't be misread as "AI can now generate scripts."

## Two things worth flagging

1. `dev` moved ahead mid-task (ATS-101's review passed). I merged it into my branch first, resolved the binary `WBS.xlsx` conflict by re-basing on `dev`'s version and replaying only my row — otherwise ATS-101's 已完成 status would have regressed to 待审核.
2. I found and fixed my own error before submitting: the docs claimed 24 error codes, the code has 25. Corrected in a separate commit with regenerated checksums.

Branch `agent/m3/seikoist-200` at `028154b` (base `e2868ed` preserved), merged `--no-ff` into `dev` at `0f52347` — trees verified identical. WBS row set to 待审核 / 完成率 1 / 剩余 0; the comment is posted and the issue is assigned to Opus with status `in_review`. I did not mark it done.

Everything is verified. Here's what I did.

## What changed

**1. ATS-101 (SEIKOIST-146) — Opus PASS, now `done`**

The 8th review round returned PASS: Opus independently reproduced both required fixes (the 5-group `grep -c` counting, and the corrected meaning of cargo's exit 101). It verified 14 verdict outputs, 5 self-written edge stubs, CHECKSUMS 76/76, `npm test` 20/20, and all syntax checks.

Opus asked the executor to sync the WBS row. I did that surgically — in the xlsx only 2 of 14 parts changed, with exactly 2 value changes (`待审核`→`已完成`, overview counter0→1). `完成率` and `剩余人日` formulas are untouched. Merged to `dev` (`ebd3859`); CHECKSUMS regenerated to 77 entries, 77/77 blob-verified.

**2. Replaced the serial stage chain with dependency-driven release — the core fix**

The old design armed `--until-children-done --stage N` on the parent. That condition means *"stages 1..N are ALL closed"*, so it serialised the five chains that the WBS dependency column says are independent. I proved the alternative on an isolated fixture first: a rule on the **dependent** child waiting on `--until-issue <prerequisite> --until-issue-state ended` fires ~60s after the prerequisite closes and dispatches a work run.

All **135 dependency edges** are now armed (audited 135/135, 0 missing) and the 32 old stage rules are disabled.

**3. Parallel work is actually running**

5 of 89 tasks are live with active runs — and one of them, ATS-102, was **auto-released by the chain itself** when ATS-101 passed. That was a production trigger, not a test.

## Two bugs I introduced and fixed

- The first instruction text said "promote to `todo`" and "don't skip dependencies" in the same breath — contradictory, and it would have started multi-prerequisite tasks early. Rewritten to 135 rules that treat a single edge as a *partial* release signal.
- A batch `wakeup create` silently dropped one edge on a TLS timeout. The audit tool caught it; I re-armed it.

## Not verified

- The "don't start early on a partial release" rule is only guaranteed at the instruction level so far. The first real multi-prerequisite task (ATS-104, needs ATS-102 + ATS-103) will exercise it.
- No Docker on this machine, so container/VM tasks (ATS-415, ATS-516) can't run locally.

Added a mode→shape mapping table to the probe README. `git grep -E '四种形态|五种失败形态|四种失败形态'` → 0 hits.

**Fix 2 — verdict now classifies by exit code.** The (b) branch didn't check the exit code, so any non-zero failure without `linking with` was reported as "compile error, or a rustc crash". Added `classify_cargo_exit`: only **101** may be called a compile error/rustc crash; **126/127** → "cargo could not start" (shell's codes, not cargo's); **any other non-zero** → "cargo/toolchain did not run normally (exit N), no build verdict".
